programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The Great British Baking Show has reached the Grand Final. After 7 gruelling weeks the three finalists; Holly, Jo and Mary-Anne face their biggest challenge yet - baking for The Great British Baking Show's street party. Only one can be crowned Britain’s Best Amateur Baker and take home the trophy

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Catch up with the bakers from series two of The Great British Baking Show. What was it really like to compete in the tent, be judged by Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, and comforted by Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins? And how has their shared love of baking and appearing on the series changed their lives?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The first episode is all about cake. To keep hold of their place in the Baking Show tent the bakers attempt to produce a showstopping cake revealing a hidden design when it is sliced in to. But who will impress the judges and become Star Baker and who will be the first to leave The Great British Baking Show?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: From the off the atmosphere in the Baking Show tent is charged as 11 bakers attempt to make flatbreads, 8 strand plaited loaf and 12 sweet and 12 savoury bagels in he showstopper challenge. But who will impress and be named Star Baker and who will fail to make the grade and have to leave.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Things are hotting up in the Baking show tent in Ep 3 as the remaining 10 bakers do their best to wow Paul and Mary with unusual flavour combinations for their tartes tartin. Produce a treacle tart technical and a showstopping tart. Who will win Star Baker and whose time in the tent has come to an end.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: This week the bakers get their just dessert as they face 3 challenges all designed for a sweet tooth. Starting off with a tempting array of decadently rich tortes, the bakers then face the technical challenge, crème caramel and finish off with a mighty showstopping layered meringue.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers turn their attention to pies and master a perfect wellington and hand raised pies. With several bakers in the danger zone, everything rests on the showstopper challenge - American pies. Who will be this week's star-spangled baker and who will be leaving the baking tent?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers go all out to impress Mary and Paul with two types of delicious sponge puddings. The technical challenge sees them face a Queen Of Pudding, a recipe direct from the archives of the Queen of Bakes, Mary Berry. And finally a Showstopping strudel that stretches the bakers to their limit

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Last week, after an accident with a food processor there are still 7 bakers left, but tonight 2 must go. This week is sweet dough recipes, including a signature regional bun challenge, a surprise technical jam doughnut recipe and a showstopping enriched dough loaf fit for a celebration

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s the biscuit based quarter final, and Paul and Mary are testing the bakers as they attempt to deliver a huge batch of perfectly baked crispbreads in the signature. The bakers have very little instructions to produce tempered chocolate tea cakes and build a showstopper from biscuits.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: There are only four bakers left vying for a place in the much sought after final of the Great British Baking show. The weight of the occasion is getting to the most unflappable of the bakers as they frantically work against the clock to deliver petits fours to Paul and Mary’s exacting standards.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: After weeks of pastries, cakes and bread, 3 Bakers have made it to the final. But they face the most demanding of challenges yet as every aspect of their baking skill is scrutinised. After 2 days of baking, whowill claim the title, winner of The Great British Baking show?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Catch up with the bakers from series three of The Great British Baking Show. What was it really like to compete in the tent, be judged by Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, and comforted by Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins? And how has their shared love of baking and appearing on the series changed their lives?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: With a range of baking styles and personalities, the tent is packed with the best amateur bakers from around the country. The judges test the bakers skills with a sandwich cake challenge, ask them to produce an Angel Food Cake with the bare bones of a recipe and create a chocolate Showstopper.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining 12 bakers having survived cake, this week they battle bread, produce 36 perfectly thin and crispy signature bread sticks, a technically tricky English Muffin, and the most outrageous showstopping loaves of bread. Who will rise to the challenge and who’s will sink and leave the tent.

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Jo Brand, Stephen K Amos and comedy duo Watson and Oliver are the first four to arrive in the tent. Facing signature shortbread as well as a dastardly technical challenge of custard slices and a showstopping portrait cake, they will be tested to the limit. But who will claim tonight's coveted title?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Mel Giedroyc welcomes Warwick Davis, Duncan Bannatyne, Simon Reeve and Andy Akinwolere into the tent to try their hand at signature iced biscuits and attempt pastry for the first time. One of them will also bake the smallest cake ever seen in the tent.

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: In this episode, Olympian Ellie Simmonds battles it out with Kirsty Wark, Julia Bradbury and Bob Mortimer over signature scones, technically tricky chocolate eclairs and a show stopping novelty cake. Who will impress the judges enough to claim tonight's title of star baker?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: In this final episode, Claudia Winkleman, Ed Byrne, Martha Kearney and Olympian Helen Glover try to impress the judges in the last round. The celebrities attempt signature chocolate biscuits, get to grips with a family size lemon meringue pie and create a showstopping birthday cake.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s week three and the bakers are juggling a Signature Trifle combining biscuit, cake, jelly or custard in perfectly distinct layers; a technically difficult task of making perfectly Floating Islands and a Showstopper that pulls out all the stops, getting the bakers to juggle 24 petit fours

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s pie and tart week. The home bakers signature double-crusted fruit pie present a challenge, the technical custard tart creates a wobble for the bakers and the showstopper sorts the bakers from the boys, as they set about making a filo pie centrepiece. on your marks...get set...BAKE!

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Almost half way through the competition and the remaining bakers are faced with biscuits and traybakes. Mel and Sue follow the trail of biscuit crumbs as the bakers produce architectural feats inspired by everything from ancient Japanese civilization to one of time travel’s most feared enemies.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s week six in the tent and time for sweet dough week. This week the bakers face Paul’s most twisted Technical Challenge yet and a Showstopper that draws on all of Europe for inspiration, creating 36 sweet European buns; from Swedish cinnamon buns to German Schnecken and French brioches.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining six bakers bring the old fashioned suet pudding bang up to date in the signature challenge, Mary Berry asks the bakers to produce 8 perfect religieuse, delicate choux buns filled with crème patissiere, and in the showstopper they must make three different types of puffed pastry.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s the quarter finals and just five bakers remain. The judges test the bakers with a signature challenge to produce a loaf using non traditional wheat flours, tested in the technical with a dacquoise recipe and pushed outside their comfort zone to create showstopping novelty vegetables cakes.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the Semi final and there are just four bakers left. This time it is the French round, and the challenges include savour canapes an opera cake and a Charlotte Royale. Whilst Mel travels to the Paris Opera House to discover where the dessert originated. Whose will hit the right note with the judges?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the final of The Great British Baking Show! 13,000 applicants were narrowed down to 13 of Britain's best amateur bakers, and the 13 became three. There are just three final challenges standing between the three bakers and the title of WINNER of the Great British Baking Show.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: We catch up with last year's bakers, who have come a long way since their time in the tent. This programme looks back at the golden moments - and recurring nightmares - of the bakers dozen from last year, as they revisit their time in the tent and share their memories

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: As they enter the tent for the very first time, the baker’s first Signature Challenge is to make a swiss roll. The Technical Challenge is Mary’s recipe for a classic cherry cake. In the Showstopper. The bakers must make classic British cakes... in perfect miniature... all 36 of them...

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining 11 bakers are tested on biscuits. The bakers must push themselves on flavour to create biscuits that go well with a cheese course. In the technical challenge Mary sets the bakers her recipe for Florentines. And the bakers are challenged to create three-dimensional biscuit scenes.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining bakers brave bread and bake 12 perfect rye bread rolls in the signature challenge. In the technical challenge, Paul tells them to 'be patient' with his recipe for ciabatta loaves. Finally, the bakers are tasked to make a filled centrepiece loaf that will have an impact on a table

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s dessert week, the bakers must bake saucy puds - delicate sponges hiding a gooey saucy filling. For the technical challenge, Mary sets her tiramisu cake. For their final flourish, the bakers are challenged to bake incredible show-stopping baked alaskas made up of cake, meringue and ice cream

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining bakers are facing pies and tarts. a signature custard tart that gives more than one of them a wobble. Paul sets the bakers mini pear pies in the technical challenge. Finally, the baker have just four hours to create a towering collection of pies from any pastry.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: For the signature challenge the bakers make yeast-leavened cakes, a tricky cross between cake and bread. Mary sets the technical challenge a Swedish princess torte and the showstopper is a two-tiered contemporary version of the traditional multi-layered Hungarian cake Dobos torte.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining bakers make signature savoury parcels, ranging from pasties to samosas. Paul's technical challenge - kouign amann tests the bakers' technical ability and patience to create a yeasted pastry full of buttery sugary layers. Finally, the bakers make show-stopping eclairs creations

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the quarter-finals and the bakers make enriched sweet fruit loaves for their signature challenge. The technical challenge is a European treat filled with swirls of cinnamon and walnuts. And a show-stopper in which the bakers must make 36 show-stopping doughnuts of two different types.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The semi-finalists are challenged to make signature baklava. The technical challenge sees the bakers make German schichttorte cake which cooked under the grill. The show-stopper challenge raises the bar even higher. The final four bakers must bake nonstop to create two elegant entremets.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the final…just three challenges lie between them and the trophy. A signature challenge that requires the mastery of a classic pastry technique: a technical challenge with no recipe, and a show-stopper challenge that demands delivery of perfect sponge, caramel, choux pastry and petit four

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Looking back over the incredible bakes of the last series, from Luis's amazing 3D biscuit scene, via the technically challenging schichttorte to Ian's binning of his baked alaska. We hear from the bakers, share their memories and catch up with what they have been doing since.

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Sue Perkins hosts the first episode, in which cricketer Michael Vaughan, James Bond and Downton Abbey actress Samantha Bond, Harry Potter actress Bonnie Wright and broadcaster Johnny Vaughan enter the tent. Who will walk away with the Star Baker Apron?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Sue Perkins hands over the baton to Jo Brand to support the next four celebrity bakers. This time the battle is between Desert Island Discs' Kirsty Young, singer and actress Jane Horrocks, Olympic gold-medal winning long jumper Greg Rutherford and ice skating's Mr Nasty, Jason Gardiner

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Omid Djalili this time and those facing the judges are Olivier award-winning singer Michael Ball, broadcaster and co-founder of Comic Relief Emma Freud, singer and presenter Jamelia and Olympic gold-medallist Victoria Pendleton. But only one can win the Star Baker apron

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: It is Ed Byrne's turn to take up the baking baton and support the four celebrities as they face their three challenges in the tent. The bakers must make pizzas for their signature challenge, eccles cakes in the technical challenge and showstopping tiered cakes that represent sporting equipment.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo is joined by Roisin Conaty, Paul Rankin and Gregg Wallace to discuss the 12 new bakers and their bakes. What do the panel think of the bakers' Swiss roll? And how did they fare with Mary Berry's cherry cake? Whose 36 miniature cakes stopped the show? Plus lots of 'exclusive' footage from the tent.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined by three celebrity fans - chef Monica Galetti, actress Lisa Faulkner and comedian Charlie Baker to discuss the 11 bakers and their biscuit bakes. Jo looks at the good, bad and the soggy bottomed, with chat, unseen footage and an interview with the week’s eliminated.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo and her panel of celebrity fans: Julian Clary, Richard Coles and Rosemary Shrager, discuss the ten bakers and the bread they have baked. What do the panel think of the bakers' rye rolls? How did they fare with the technical challenge - ciabatta? And whose filled centrepiece loaf stood out?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand and three celebrity fans highlights from the tent, with chat, unseen footage and an interview with the week's eliminated baker. Comedian Roisin Conaty, chef Glynn Purnell and former contestant Howard Middleton look back at one of the most sensational episodes of Baking Show yet.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is pies and tarts week in the tent, so Jo and her panel of celebrity fans: Chef Michel Roux Jr, comedian Shappi Khorsandi and former home secretary Alan Johnson continue the theme in the An Extra Slice studio, looking at audience bakes and viewer photos - the good, the bad and the disastrous.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is European cake week in the tent, so Jo and her panel of fans celebrate them by tasting audience bakes and looking at viewer photos of bakes from home - the triumphs and the tragedies. Actress Fay Ripley, comedian Romesh Ranganathan and chef Richard Corrigan are Jo Brand's guests in the studio

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is pastries week in the tent, which means Jo Brand and her panel of celebrity fans are celebrating anything and everything to do with pastry. In the studio, the panel looks at bakes brought in by the audience and viewer photos of their bakes from home - the delectable and the downright disastrous.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined by Hairy Biker Dave Myers, author Marian Keyes and comedian Hal Cruttenden to look back at advanced dough week. Who do they think shone making doughnuts in the show-stopper? And who do they think will make the final three and eventually be crowned winner?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined by chef Tom Aikens, actress Fay Ripley and comedian Josh Widdicombe. What do the panel have to say about the bakers' signature baklavas? How did the bakers cope with making entremets for the show-stopper? The panel also give their best guesses at who will be crowned winner.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand looks back at the final with Paul Hollywood, Mary Berry and all of the year's bakers, including the newly-crowned Champion. Jo interviews this year's champion, the two runners-up and is joined by all of this year's bakers. Plus, there’s unseen footage and a look at viewer and audience bakes

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: 12 new bakers head for the Baking Show tent. Judges Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood have created 3 challenges that will test their baking prowess. Starting with cake week, the bakers make a madeira cake, are tested with a frosted walnut cake and try to impress with a black forest gateau showstopper.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: This week the remaining bakers tackle biscuits. The signature challenge is to create 24 biscotti. Paul chooses the technical challenge, arlettes, a French reverse puff pastry biscuit. And finally, the show-stopper is to build an edible biscuit box filled with 36 biscuits of a different flavour

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The ten remaining bakers must make quick breads – they have an hour and a half to get creative with their flavours. Paul sets baguettes as the technical challenge. A seemingly simple recipe or is it? For their show-stopper, the bakers must make edible 3D bread sculptures

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: For the nine bakers left, it's time to tackle desserts. The signature challenge comes in the form of a French classic - creme brulee. Mary picks the technical challenge - the spanische windtorte from Austria. Three baked cheesecakes make up the final show-stopper challenge

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The remaining bakers must bake without sugar, gluten or dairy. The bakers create a variety of sugar-free cakes and use honey, agave syrup and fruit. Paul picks the technical challenge, gluten-free pittas. For their show-stopper, the bakers must make dairy-free ice cream rolls.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers prove their skill with pastry by making frangipane tarts for their signature challenge. The technical challenge is a cheese-filled pastry from Cyprus - the flaouna. The show-stopper is the classic 70s canape, vol-au-vents: bitesize puff pastry stuffed with tasty fillings

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers go back to the Victorian era and make a dinner table staple, the game pie. The bakers then make a perfect fruit cake that resembles a tennis court. For the show-stopper, the bakers make charlotte russe, a dessert with a silky bavarois centre surrounded by sponge fingers and topped with jelly

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: No series of Baking Show would be complete without testing the bakers on patisserie, and what better time to do it than the quarter-finals? The five remaining bakers must work their way through childhood favourites and delicate french fancies to a mountainous choux pastry masterpiece.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It's the semi-finals and the remaining bakers must get to grips with chocolate. They revisit their old friend pastry for a chocolate tart signature, Mary sets a technical challenge to make a chocolate souffle. And the bakers create spectacular chocolate centrepieces for their showstopper.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: Three finalists and three final challenges. The bakers create delicious filled iced buns in the signature. The technical requires them to conquer something they’ve all struggled with, and for their showstopper, they make a classic British cake. Who will hold their nerve and be crowned the winner

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The bakers from Series 6 return to the tent for a special look back. A lot has happened in the year since they hung up their aprons. They share their memories, relive their highlights of the series and reveal what they are up to now.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Kicking off the series, Jo and her panel of Celebrity fans will give us their take on the 12 new bakers. Will they go mad for the bakers' madeira cake? How do they think the dozen coped with their first technical bake - Mary's frosted walnut cake? Whose black forest gateau show-stopper stopped the show?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It's biscuit week, so Jo and her celebrity guests celebrate all sorts of biscuits, tasting audience attempts at cookies and crackers and looking at viewer photos of their bakes from home. They’ll also be unseen footage from the tent and chat with the eliminated baker.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It's bread week, so Jo and guests Deborah Meaden, Richard Bertinet and Josh Widdicombe cast their eyes over the home-baked breads brought in by the studio audience. They also look through photos of viewers' home baking efforts and chat to the eliminated baker.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Joining host Jo Brand are three celebrity fans - Glynn Purnell, Liza Tarbuck and Henning Wehn - who dissect this week's action from the Bake Off tent. As well as lots of witty chat and exclusive footage from the tent and there's an interview with the latest baker to leave.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Judy Murray, Michael Caines and Hal Cruttenden join Jo Brand to give their take on this week's sugar- and gluten-free Bake Off shenanigans.Jo and her guests also taste bakes brought in by the audience, also look at photos of viewer bakes from home - the good, the bad and the downright catastrophic

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: The first brave celebrities to enter the Bake Off Tent are four of the most iconic figures in British entertainment - Joanna Lumley, Jennifer Saunders, Lulu, and Dame Edna Everage - who has come out retirement especially for Comic Relief. They must take on three challenges set by Mary and Paul

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Mel Giedroyc welcomes four more celebrities into the tent to test out their baking expertise. They are Gok Wan, Jonathan Ross, Abbey Clancy and Zoe Sugg - also known as internet sensation Zoella. Who will impress legendary cookery writer Mary Berry and acclaimed master baker Paul Hollywood?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: In the third episode Jo Brand welcomes four more celebrities into the tent to lay bare their baking skills. They are David Mitchell, Michael Sheen, Radio 1 DJ Jameela Jamil and Sarah Brown. Tensions are high and confusion is rife, but who will impress and who will miss the mark?

programme.title: Celebrity Baking Show
programme.desc: Ed Byrne welcomes Victoria Wood, Alexa Chung, Chris Moyles and Kayvan Novak to the tent. They face three tricky challenges set by Mary and Paul.Who will demonstrate baking brilliance and be crowned star baker?

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Joining host Jo Brand in the An Extra Slice studio are three celebrity fans - Marcus Wareing, Marian Keyes and Rob Beckett - all eager to chew over pastry week in the tent.Jo and her guests taste audience bakes and look at viewer photos of their home bakes - from tantalising tarts to pitiful pastries.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: It is week seven and just six bakers remain. Joining host Jo Brand in the An Extra Slice studio are three celebrity Bake Off fans - Michel Roux Jnr, David Baddiel and historian Ruth Goodman - eager to chew over the latest goings-on in the tent. An Extra Slice – perfect if you can’t resist a second helping.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Sarah Millican stands in and is joined by Gregg Wallace, Joe Lycett and pastry chef Cherish Finden to dissect the events in the tent, with unseen footage and an interview with eliminated baker. They also taste bakes brought in by the studio audience and look at viewer photos of their bakes from home

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined by celebrity fans - Danny Baker, Josh Widdicombe and Tom Aikens - to dissect how the bakers tackled chocolate. As well as unseen footage Jo and the panel taste bakes by the studio audience and look at photos viewers home bakes. Jo interviews the last baker to leave before the final

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show:An Extra Slice
programme.desc: Jo Brand is joined in the studio by Paul Hollywood and Mary Berry to get their take on the nerve-wracking final bakes and how and why they chose their eventual winner. Jo will interview the champion, the two runners-up and will be joined by all of this year's bakers. Plus a look at the audience bakes too.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: The competition begins with a British classic and Mary's technical challenge - a popular cake with a fatless sponge and tricky chocolate work. Finally, the bakers show the judges what they can do with their showstopper. One baker will be crowned star baker, one contestant will be leaving the tent.

programme.title: The Great British Baking Show
programme.desc: It’s biscuit week and the bakers signature challenge is to make 24 identical decorated biscuits. The technical challenge requires perfect piping to avoid a crumbling whirl. The showstopper requires precision baking to build a biscuit structure that reveals a little more about each of the bakers

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Drill Charging Station
programme.desc: Back in 2010 I built a Drill Charging Station to show off a new joinery gadget. It was really simple and didn't quite have a feature set outside of being two shelves on the wall. So only eight short years later I finally decided to build a proper Drill Charging Station, made from Baltic Birch plywood featuring all the storage I need for 5 drills, two chargers, and all of my bits and accessories.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: DIY Kids School Desk - Quick - Easy - Inexpensive!
programme.desc: A one-day build using 1/4 sheet of plywood and a 2x4.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Knock Down Trestle Table Part 1
programme.desc: The table is a trestle design which keeps the legs out of the way and gives us plenty of overhang. The joinery is all mortise and tenon including some cool double wedged mortise and tenon joints. I even added extra supports in the middle of the table that will not only support the top but should also help keep the table top flat over time.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Woven Panel Rolling Hamper Part 2
programme.desc: The hamper is assembled, hinges are added, casters are attached, finish is applied, and snaps are installed on the cotton bags.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Tricked Out Bandsaws Featuring Carter Products
programme.desc: The bandsaw is one of my favorite tools and if you treat it well, it will quickly become one of your favorites as well. While most modern bandsaws come with decent components, to begin with, there are companies like Carter Products who make high-quality after-market add-ons that can make your bandsaw better performing and easier to adjust. One of the best upgrades you can do is replacing the guide

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Cutting Thin Strips at the Table Saw
programme.desc: Resawing thin stock and cutting thin strips is typically the domain of the bandsaw. And while I consider the bandsaw to be an essential shop tool, not everyone has one. So it's probably worth considering an alternative option that kills two birds with one stone: utilizing a more common tool that results in a smoother cut.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Protecting Outdoor Furniture with Epoxy Feet
programme.desc: Mother Nature always wins. So when you make outdoor furniture you have two choices: commit to a regular maintenance schedule or come to terms with the weathered gray look. An easy thing you can do to help the cause is to prevent moisture from entering into the legs. This simple trick requires nothing more than epoxy and masking tape.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Trestle Table Part 2
programme.desc: Now that the leg pieces are cut to their rough shape, we need to focus on blending the parts using an assortment of tools including a router, a ball mill, and a cabinet-maker’s rasp. You’ll notice that much of the sculpting work is done before the glueup. I find it much easier to work on these parts in smaller pieces rather than trying to work the entire finished leg at once.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: AWFS 2007 Special - Part 1 of 2
programme.desc: Special episode of The Wood Whisperer on location at AWFS fair in Los Vegas!

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Interview with Kaleo Kala
programme.desc: A chat with woodworker and designer, Kaleo Kala.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Buy This Not That - Measuring and Marking
programme.desc: Tools I think you should buy as well as tools I think you should avoid.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Bit Storage Cabinet
programme.desc: A wall-hanging cabinet to help you organize and store your drill and router bits.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: 60 Seconds to Sharp
programme.desc: Most videos about sharpening, including my own, focus on how to tune up an old tool or properly set a new one. Thankfully, once you do that process it isn't likely you'll have to do it again for a very long time. From that point on, you'll be sharpening in maintenance mode.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: You Don't Need Breadboard Ends - Ask TWW
programme.desc: You don't need breadboard ends - and that's why.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Urea Resin Woodworking Glues
programme.desc: We take a look at urea resin woodworking glues. These glues definitely have their advantages: low water content, gap-filling, long open time, and rigid glue lines just to name a few. But keep in mind the one big disadvantage: safety. These glues are pretty nasty and you might be best served considering other options. But with proper precautions, this glue can be a nice addition to your shop.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Don’t Make These Lumber Mistakes!
programme.desc: A few tips that will make your life easier when buying and using lumber and plywood.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Lumber Rack aka Racking My Brain
programme.desc: The lumber rack is the unsung hero of the woodworking shop. Its responsible for holding our raw materials safely, securely, and in an organized fashion until we're ready to use them.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Making Raised Panel Doors aka Raising Arizona
programme.desc: Every well-rounded woodworker should know how to make raised panels doors! In this episode, Marc help you to learn or refresh your memory on making cool panel doors.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Crooked Garden Gate
programme.desc: Building a garden gate for a space that's anything but square.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: A $35 Hand Plane? Ask TWW
programme.desc: Thoughts on Grizzly's planes? Coping Sleds. Problem with Tung Oil Finish. Fesool Sanders 3 vs 5 Stroke How to Soundproof the Shop. What are your greatest influences? Glue for Vacuum Pressing. Filling Epoxy Gaps Is Carbon Filtration Helpful? Is CNC a novelty?

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: VerySuperCool Tools After-Market Tablesaw Fence
programme.desc: The guys over at VerySuperCool Tools recently gave me an opportunity to test out one of their new products: an after-market fence system. The great thing about this unit is that it works perfectly with existing Biesemeyer-style fences. So installation is as simple as dropping it on the rail and performing a standard fence calibration.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: A Better Way to Apply Oil Finishes!
programme.desc: Applying oil finishes sparingly is the key to avoiding problems with curing and other flaws in the surface.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Rubbing Out a High Gloss Finish
programme.desc: One of the biggest challenges woodworkers face is getting a nice smooth blemish-free finish. Let's face it, very few of us have spray booths and our shops are far from ideal finishing environments. It's to be expected that our finish will nearly always have dust and other pieces of debris residing within it. Fortunately, there is a way that just about any finish can be improved.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Crooked Garden Gate

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: A $35 Hand Plane? Ask TWW
programme.desc: Thoughts on Grizzly's planes? Coping Sleds. Problem with Tung Oil Finish. Fesool Sanders 3 vs 5 Stroke How to Soundproof the Shop. What are your greatest influences? Glue for Vacuum Pressing. Filling Epoxy Gaps Is Carbon Filtration Helpful? Is CNC a novelty?

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: VerySuperCool Tools After-Market Tablesaw Fence
programme.desc: The guys over at VerySuperCool Tools recently gave me an opportunity to test out one of their new products: an after-market fence system. The great thing about this unit is that it works perfectly with existing Biesemeyer-style fences. So installation is as simple as dropping it on the rail and performing a standard fence calibration.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: A Better Way to Apply Oil Finishes!
programme.desc: Applying oil finishes sparingly is the key to avoiding problems with curing and other flaws in the surface.

programme.title: The Wood Whisperer: Rubbing Out a High Gloss Finish
programme.desc: One of the biggest challenges woodworkers face is getting a nice smooth blemish-free finish. Let's face it, very few of us have spray booths and our shops are far from ideal finishing environments. It's to be expected that our finish will nearly always have dust and other pieces of debris residing within it. Fortunately, there is a way that just about any finish can be improved.

programme.title: Secret Wars Uncovered S1 - "Desert War In Mali"
programme.desc: It is a deadly war in the desert, one we know barely anything about. Once the heart of the golden Mali Empire, home to the richest man of the 14th century, the northern town of Timbuktu has become the victim of political instability and terror.

programme.title: Battle Factory S1 - "An Assault Rifle, a Bomb Suit, a Mortar, and a Zodiac"
programme.desc: What starts off as a seven-pound bar of solid steel will soon deliver a bullet with deadly accuracy when it becomes the barrel of a Colt C7 assault rifle, and when plastic and bulletproof fabric are molded and stitched together,they’ll make a suit of armour made for the most dangerous job in the world.

programme.title: Battle Factory S1 - "A Parajet, a Hovercraft, a Camo Jacket, and a Portable Military Shelter"
programme.desc: As lightweight aluminum is cut and tooled, it will become the frame of a personal flying machine. Used by military operatives, drug enforcement agents, and first responders – it gets you in and out fast, whether you are carrying a camera or a gun.

programme.title: Battle Factory S1 - "A Sniper Rifle, a Zeppelin, a Ka-Bar Knife, and Dragon Eggs"
programme.desc: In 48 hours, a block of metal will be formed into the most accurate weapon on earth: the AX-338 Sniper Rifle. In a warzone, police stand off, or hostage taking, the sniper is often the only solution to a bad situation.

programme.title: Combat Forces S1 - "Artillery"
programme.desc: Artillery, the King of Battle, is explored as gunners train with powerful weapons and prepare for modern combat deployment.

programme.title: Combat Forces S1 - "First Ten Combat Missions"
programme.desc: During the Vietnam War, the USAF learned most pilot losses happened in their first 10 missions, leading to intense training that saves lives.

programme.title: Strip The City S2 - "Los Angeles"
programme.desc: Stripping Los Angeles to its core, CGI reveals the hidden steel and fault lines that help this earthquake-prone city survive "the Big One."

programme.title: Strip The City S2 - "New Orleans"
programme.desc: CGI peels back the Superdome and the city’s silt to reveal the massive pumps and barriers keeping New Orleans from sinking.

programme.title: Strip The City S2 - "New York"
programme.desc: Dissecting New York's stone and steel, CGI reveals the inflatable subway plugs and bedrock foundations shielding the city from Atlantic superstorms.

programme.title: Made in Britain S1 - "Whitaker's Chocolates and Heck! Sausages"
programme.desc: Lord Prescott visits Whitaker’s chocolate factory to explore large-scale chocolate making, from factory lines to expert tasting and the company’s rich history. He then heads to HECK! Sausages in North Yorkshire, where he attempts to create his own custom recipe—the Hull banger.

programme.title: Made in Britain S1 - "Wensleydale Cheese and Mowbray Pork Pies"
programme.desc: At the Wensleydale Creamery, Lord Prescott joins master cheesemakers to follow the production of the famous Yorkshire Wensleydale cheese, learning the art of cheese-tasting along the way. His next stop is Mowbray Pork Pies, where he experiences the high-speed world of pie production.

programme.title: Made in Britain S1 - "Lea and Perrins Worcestershire Sauce and Soreen's Malt Loaf"
programme.desc: Exploring the historic Lea & Perrins factory, Lord Prescott uncovers the story behind its legendary Worcestershire sauce, made since 1837. He then heads to Manchester to the Soreen factory, home of the beloved malt loaf, where he joins the production line and experiments with creating a new flavour.

programme.title: Made in Britain S1 - "Ambrosia's desserts and Young's battered fish"
programme.desc: To discover how his favourite meal—fish supper followed by rice pudding—is made, Lord Prescott visits the Ambrosia factory in Devon to explore the production of classic British desserts. Returning north to Grimsby, he heads to the Young's factory to learn about their famous fish pie.

programme.title: Strip The Cosmos S1 - "The Sun"
programme.desc: By stripping away the Sun's boiling plasma layers, this CGI study reveals the nuclear core that fuels our world while tracking lethal solar storms.

programme.title: Strip The Cosmos S1 - "Alien Worlds"
programme.desc: A virtual scalpel dissects methane lakes and icy crusts to reveal hidden oceans and water-erupting volcanoes on distant moons.

programme.title: Strip The Cosmos S1 - "Asteroids"
programme.desc: By stripping the crust and peeling back craters, CGI exposes the hidden minerals and refueling potential locked inside these asteroid worlds.

programme.title: Strip The Cosmos S1 - "Black Holes"
programme.desc: Stripping away cosmic layers with CGI, this film reveals how black holes act as both destructive abysses and vital anchors for our galaxy.

programme.title: GLORY Kickboxing
programme.desc: GLORY Kickboxing’s Summer of GLORY concluded with a massive event from the Johan Cruijff Arena in Amsterdam. In the night’s headliner, heavyweight champion Rico Verhoeven took on Brazilian challenger Guto Inocente. Verhoeven had defended his belt seven straight times since capturing the title in 2014. His winning streak inside the GLORY ring stood at 16. Inocente looked to dethrone the world’s top-ranked heavyweight riding the momentum of wins over Benjamin Adegbuyi, D’Angelo Marshall and Hesdy Gerges. Gold was also on the line in the co-main event, as longtime featherweight titleholder Robin van Roosmalen rematched interim champion Petchpanomrung Kiatmookao. The pair met previously at GLORY 41 — also in van Roosmalen’s home country of Holland — with the Dutchman taking home a controversial, majority-decision victory.

programme.title: The Cast
programme.desc: Recognized as the GOAT of the sport, Kevin VanDam came on the scene and dominated in every way with 4 Bassmaster Classic Titles and 7 Angler of the Year wins. KVD was always in contention for championships and holds the record for most professional wins at 25.

programme.title: The Cast
programme.desc: Texas has consistently hosted B.A.S.S. events with some of the most memorable and iconic fish catches in the history of tournament bass fishing.

programme.title: The Cast
programme.desc: People recognize Davy today as one of the most important voices in the sport of Bass Fishing. Davy’s experience on the water though, produced 8 professional level wins including 2 Angler of the Year titles and 1 Bassmaster Classic.

programme.title: The Cast
programme.desc: Considered one of the most prestigious awards in the sport of professional Bass fishing, this episode highlights what it takes to be a consistent champion in the highest level of professional bass fishing.

programme.title: The Cast
programme.desc: The B.A.S.S. Federation has been the heartbeat of the sport. It has been and always will be the way for weekend warriors to compete and possibly win on the biggest stage.

programme.title: The Cast
programme.desc: Some of the biggest changes in the sport happened starting in the late 90s and into the new millennium. The way the sport was covered and viewed on television exploded to new levels never seen before.

programme.title: The Cast
programme.desc: Revered by many as “The Natural” in professional bass fishing, Aaron Martens brought a unique approach to the sport reaching the highest level. 3 Angler of the Year Titles and 9 Professional level wins proved his techniques were quite effective in the sport.

programme.title: Peak Performance - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: In this Marathon Peak Performance, we take a look at Brandon Palaniuk's amazing 2022 season en route to his second Angler of the Year title.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Greg Hackney
programme.desc: Greg Hackney gives some love to an often-forgotten lure for smallmouth fishing and that is the good ole fashioned tube. Hackney still appreciates what a tube brings to the table while fishing for smallmouth on competition days.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Timothy Dube
programme.desc: Tim Dube walks us through one of his favorite techniques in tournaments and fun fishing. Dube gives his take on practicing with a Glide Bait and his strategy to convert followers into fish that will commit to biting.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cody Huff
programme.desc: Cody Huff explores the benefits he's found when using various spoons during the late summer. He has dialed in his setups and doesn't experiment with multiple brands of spoons but rather uses the same spoons and changes sizes based on situation. From a magnum spoon to a compact jigging spoon Huff has found success on these from the Tennessee River to the Ozarks and many places in between.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Austin Felix
programme.desc: Austin Felix gives his thoughts on when he picks up a Dropshot versus a Ned Rig and a Neko Rig. Speed is often the determining factor for each presentation and he tends to reserve the Neko for largemouth situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jake Whitaker
programme.desc: Jake Whitaker talks about the shallow bite windows that open up even with 100 degree days in the south. Whitaker leans on a topwater toad around any sort of cover that could hold fish. Anglers may get less bites in the heat of the summer but they can be the quality you need in a tournament.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie discusses the tricky period immediately after bass leave the bed and are either guarding fry or recovering from the spawn. Here is how Christie opts to catch them.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bernie Schultz
programme.desc: Florida pro Bernie Schultz talks buzzbaits specifically two kinds. He keeps a squeaking buzzbait and clacking buzzbait ready to go at all times especially in the post-spawn. Although it's an excellent technique in the post-spawn Schultz acknowledges its use early in the year in places like Florida Texas and other southern states. Buzz it slow or fast make it clack or squeak add a toad or a trailer hook whatever you'd like with a buzzbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Patrick Walters
programme.desc: Elite Series Champion Patrick Walters gives the details of his approach at Lake Murray. Walters relied on a few baits throughout the week to win the event wire to wire. When fish were active and schooling Walters utilized a Zoom Super Fluke and a Rapala Jowler.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brad Whatley
programme.desc: Brad Whatley gives his strategy of covering water around the spawn when there is thicker cover present. Whatley winds his weighted swimbait around spawning areas and will trigger strikes or boils revealing where bass are positioned to catch on another tactic if necessary.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Parks
programme.desc: Logan Parks discusses a strategy he employed at Wheeler during his first Top 10. Varying line size can help crankbaits run different depth and retrieved faster or slower. It's something he recommends during the summer months when schools are forming offshore or have been fished for frequently.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Easton Fathergill
programme.desc: Easton Fothergill gives his daily adjustment to how fish were positioned each day of the Classic. From windy days to calm moments Fothergill kept adjusting his tackle to maximize efficiency.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen goes through two baits he always has rigged up this time of year. A tube and a jig are staples in Lowen's boat and he explains how both get fished in conjunction with one another. There are a few variables like pegging his weight or letting it free flow and also line size in these situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyoya Fujita
programme.desc: Kyoya Fujita gives the specifics of his lures that helped him win at Toledo Bend. Fujita was using a technique called "mid-strolling" to get his Jackall Drift Fry and his Deps Sakamata Shad to the correct depth to target suspended bass.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Justin Atkins
programme.desc: Justin Atkins sheds light on the flats. A vast area of consistent contour depths and also a place where baitfish and bass congregate as the season turns to cooler temperatures in the fall. This can be a great landing spot for bass as they get positioned to feed during this time of year.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock explains a new bait he was introduced to that helps him catch not only deep northern smallmouth but also southern largemouth in the winter months. He also discusses the value in 2D sonar with this technique around structure in the south.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Latuso
programme.desc: Logan Latuso discusses a big key in the summer months...SHADE. This underrated aspect of the summer can get you some of the biggest bites of your day and it seemingly gets better as the day progresses. Take notes from Latuso and don't run your shade pattern too early to ensure some of your best success.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew talks about one of his favorite fun-fishing lures which is the Umbrella Rig aka Alabama Rig. LeHew utilizes this in multiple ways as he can cover water around shallow cover like he would with a spinnerbait but also with his electronics around deeper offshore structure.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Timothy Dube
programme.desc: Tim Dube discusses his use of a deep diving jerkbait to cover water depths from 4 feet out to 15 feet or so. Dube exclusively uses 10 to 12-pound line and will change his cadence from fast early in the retrieve to slower in the strike zone.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Williamson
programme.desc: Jason Williamson provides a solution to those tricky bass that are days from spawning and sit high in the water column. Not only does a jig provide great opportunities for good catches but a swimbait also entices those big females to commit.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cory Johnston
programme.desc: Cory Johnston goes over his two main lures for bed fishing at the St. Johns River en route to his first Elite Series victory. Johnston also explains his use of Perspective Mode when seeing bed fish in low visibility times.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen explains his two-pronged approach at the St. Johns River sticking to one area for four days using a black and blue swim jig and a flipping jig. He highlights his swim jig cadence and the importance of his flipping jig falling into hard cover

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Justin Hamner
programme.desc: Justin Hamner gives his strategy to catch key bass each day of competition and how he utilized multiple kinds of jerkbaits and mixed in a jig to catch the majority of his weight on Grand Lake in the 2024 Bassmaster Classic.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Arey
programme.desc: Matt Arey talks about the importance of varying your retrieve with swimbaits over structure like brush piles. This is something that can be done with or without forward facing sonar as Arey describes the trial and error used prior to newer technology.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brock Mosley
programme.desc: Brock Mosley praises the most versatile lure in bass fishing the Yamamoto Senko. He shows how you can quickly switch from fishing the Senko weightless wacky rigged to adding a weight and changing the hook positioning for a Neko Rig. This lure will get fish to bite every day of the year depending on how you rig it.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New lays out one of his favorite topwater presentations the Buzz Toad. Pioneered by his good friend and fellow Elite Todd Auten New likes to use this bait to imitate multiple types of forage bass will eat in the post-spawn.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Card
programme.desc: Brandon Card gives his thoughts on early season jerkbait fishing. Card gives scenarios when he will opt for a different cadence for his jerkbait rod length and line size.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew relies on a jerkbait from late fall through the spawn whether using electronics or not. He keeps two color options: translucent for sunny or clear water and solid for cloudy or stained conditions.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Wes Logan
programme.desc: Wes Logan talks moving water and how he approaches it. Being from the Coosa River Logan is used to fishing moving water no matter the time of year and these three baits help him have good success.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Pat Schlapper
programme.desc: Pat Schlapper recounts his finest tournament week to date where to took the title at the Sabine River. Schlapper relied on a few areas of the Sabine along with a few lures including a Do-It Molds compact jig he pours himself altering it with a smaller stouter hook. He also utilized a Brazalo Custom Lures Bushwhacker Buzz Bait in the morning on the final day when it put multiple quality fish in the boat.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Tucker Smith
programme.desc: Tucker Smith talks about finding hard spots on Lake Fork with his side imaging throughout practice and then using his forward facing sonar to execute and catch fish throughout the tournament. He utilized a 7-inch minnow on spinning tackle with varying head sizes as well as a 3/4-ounce football jig on the final day.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan New
programme.desc: Bryan New goes through some of the keys he likes in his jig when targeting bass in the prespawn. New breaks down his jig trailer and why it's efficient and also explains an adjustment to his jig size that he used to never use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock relies on burning a crankbait over grass rock and stumps during late winter and pre-spawn. He ups his line size to keep the bait higher and uses a 7'4" rod for longer casts and ripping it free from grass.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Robert Gee
programme.desc: Robert Gee reflects on his 2024 success with largemouth smallmouth and spotted bass noting that spots and smallmouth chase differently than largemouth requiring presentation adjustments. He shares his preferred head sizes go-to knot and a simple rod and reel setup most anglers can use.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Williamson
programme.desc: Jason Williamson pulls out his favorite bait for the fall when the water temperatures are falling and in many situations the water level is falling too. When the bass start keying in on crawfish with cooling water J-Will knows its jig season. With living rubber skirted jigs Williamson fishes a 1/2 ounce or 3/4 ounce jig and never goes lighter than 1/2 ounce. He will also target brush early and as it continues to cool down will move to rock through the winter.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bill Lowen
programme.desc: Bill Lowen runs down his three favorite colors for squarebill crankbaits in the fall. Another essential aspect to a squarebill that Lowen cherishes is a circuit board bill vs a plastic bill. It gives the crankbait the feel and characteristic of a balsa crankbait while maintaining the durability of a plastic crankbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Hunter Shryock
programme.desc: Hunter Shryock discusses the rising trend of using a swimbait in the prespawn as a substitute for commonly thrown baits with similar profiles. Fished around the same shallow cover it can trigger the big kicker bite tournament anglers seek.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Cobb
programme.desc: Brandon Cobb gives his top picks for effective baits on lakes with blueback herring. Spotted bass and largemouth will get hyper focused on blueback herring when they exist on a body of water and Cobb knows these baits will work throughout the year and not a certain specific season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Herren
programme.desc: Matt Herren goes through the process of fishing current seams on rivers with a spinnerbait. No matter time of year water current is a great place to find fish and target where bass are positioned and if you find the correct lineup it can be fast action. Herren recommends a 1/2-ounce to 3/4-ounce compact spinnerbait to avoid snags and hangups and control the bait despite the current pushing and washing the spinnerbait.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Greg Hackney
programme.desc: The Shad Spawn is a unique stage of the fishing season that bridges the gap from the bass spawn into the post spawn. Shad spawning around hard shallow cover gives bass a great opportunity to feed heavily in a short window of time. Not all places in the country feature a shad spawn but if threadfin are present in your lake a shad spawn is likely to happen. Low-light conditions early in the morning are helpful and baits like a spinnerbait imitate small shad perfectly to load the boat for Greg Hackney in a hurry.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Caleb Sumrall
programme.desc: Caleb Sumrall talks about one of the best ways to catch big bass. Sumrall strongly believes in a frog but when bass start shying away or missing it he downsizes instead of changing baits completely. When conditions change bass moods can vary and with that topwater becomes a high risk high reward situation and Sumrall will downsize to the keep the odds in his favor.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Alex Wetherell
programme.desc: Alex Wetherell discusses two soft plastics he uses around his home in Connecticut and down south when the calendar hits December. Balls of bait equal bass for Wetherell as they actively feed even when the water temperatures are cooler at the end of the year. Bass aren’t nearly as lethargic as we once believed years ago.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bernie Schultz
programme.desc: Bernie Schultz gives his three trusted lures when he is covering water to develop a pattern in the spring. He balances a spinnerbait swim jig and chatterbait when he approaches different types of cover.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jason Christie
programme.desc: Jason Christie discusses fishing a jerkbait around Christmas time and how two of his baits act totally different. Christie breaks down how the Smithwick Rogue and Booyah Flash Point react different on the same cadence. Water temperatures in the 40's Christie opts for the Rogue. Meanwhile he sees positive results with the quick-working Flash Point with temperatures in the 50's and even 60's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cliff Prince
programme.desc: Cliff Prince dials us in on his 1/2 ounce Chatterbait setup that helped him win the Bassmaster Elite at Wheeler Lake. He also dishes the details on his magic spot and why he thinks the morning was incredible every day for him.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kenta Kimura
programme.desc: Kenta Kimura gives some suggestions to be better with the Megabass Magdraft swimbait. He changes the treble to his signature Ryugi quad-hook design for better hookups and he also adds a split ring to the line tie for increased head action and roll. Those two things are essential for Kimura along with finding the right speed on retrieve.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Scott Martin
programme.desc: Scott Martin sets up the calendar for Florida's Spawn Cycle. Depending on weather spawn can start in south Florida as early as Thanksgiving week and extend through May of the next year. Martin gives his take on the difference of a lake like Okeechobee and the St. Johns River farther north.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt highlights how different SPRO Aruku Shad versions and hook sizes enhance performance based on season cover and action. He adjusts for fall rates with yo-yo or straight retrieves and downsizes when the bite is tough.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bob Downey
programme.desc: Bob Downey dishes out a few of his must-have baits for the early fall fishing season for Smallmouth bass. Downey who lives in Minnesota knows how incredible the bite can be this time of year before cold temps hit daily. Given the type of lake Downey has options for you in this video.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Hunter Shryock
programme.desc: Hunter Shryock talks about one of the most fun techniques and lures that is so effective in the Fall season. Covering water with a Berkley Choppo is essential and allows Shryock to burn through dead water in no time with this approach and it is a tournament winning formula.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Ed Laughran III
programme.desc: Lake Champlain Champion Ed Loughran runs through his jig setup that accounted for most of the fish throughout his tournament. He also leaned on a topwater in practice and on Championship Monday to catch smallmouth.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Patrick
programme.desc: Kyle Patrick gives his approach for fishing for less pressured fish during the spawning months of the year. The fishing myth around the spawn is that bass have to go to the bank to do their yearly spawn when in reality fish can spawn much deeper and will take longer to do so.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Taku Ito
programme.desc: Taku Ito goes through two key baits to his Bassmaster Elite Series victory at Smith Lake. From Neko Rigging a bluegill imitating bait to dropshotting a Magnum Fuzzy Dice he managed the biggest bass and bag to win.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher breaks down his single bait that produced a record winning margin and over 118 pounds of bass at the Pasquotank River. Flipping a Rapala CrushCity Bronco Bug to shallow roamers and spawning bass was his strategy. He utilized his forward facing sonar to pick out fish among the cover littered on the bottom.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Crews
programme.desc: John Crews offers a different option for enticing schooling fish to bite when it gets tough and pressured in the summer. Using a Spy Bait can offer up another look that is great for casting and mimicking baitfish.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Scott Martin
programme.desc: Scott Martin gives us his version of Thanksgiving turkey and fixings with this three-bait lineup this time of year. He has a bait for every level of the water column depending on how the fish are acting and where you're fishing this time of year.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Tyler Williams
programme.desc: Tyler Williams reveals the details to his 3/4 ounce jig he uses across the country. Upsizing his line can help slow the fall of his heavy jig along with pairing the jig with a big bulky trailer. Williams will use this jig around docks brush piles ledges and when targeting specific fish on his forward-facing sonar.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bryan Schmitt
programme.desc: Bryan Schmitt pulls 4 swim jigs out of his tackle box to showcase their effectiveness on different pieces of cover and depths. A simple trailer change can help Schmitt's swim jig stay shallow or go deeper. Schmitt gives the nuts and bolts to swim jig fishing his way and style.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Todd Auten
programme.desc: Todd Auten goes over three Chatterbait variations that have made the South Carolina pro successful with this technique. Whether it's color selection trailer options or getting the bait to ride high in the water column or fall fast Auten has his process. 1. White/CChartuese w/Zoom Shimmer Shad 2. Black/Blue w/Zoom ZCraw or Green Pumpkin Fluke 3. Firecraw w/Speed Craw

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: One of the best structure fishermen in the world Brandon Palaniuk talks about isolated structure in the fall season. BP also gives a few bait suggestions including his handy dropshot.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Palaniuk
programme.desc: Brandon Palaniuk shares the three baits he used to win the Bassmaster Elite Series at Lake Okeechobee: a Megabass Kanata jerkbait and two Megabass crankbaits (Big M and a prototype). Fishing one spot aggressively led to some of the biggest strikes seen on Bassmaster LIVE.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Trey McKinney
programme.desc: Lake Fork Champion Trey McKinney gives his lure arsenal as he adjusted daily to the changing fish for the second stop of the Elite Series season. Early in the event he used a jerkbait and jig head minnow combo but as the weather warm and conditions changed his baits adapted. Culminating on the final day were multiple baits contributed to his 130-15 tournament weight.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brandon Lester
programme.desc: Brandon Lester gives us two key factors he relies on when choosing between a Jig and Texas Rig which is often a debate in the Fall fishing season. Profile and rate of fall depending on the seasonal conditions are considerations for the two-time BASS winner.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Cox
programme.desc: John Cox gives a look at two of his favorite topwater lures and ones he trusts in the Fall. Whether it's around grass wood or rock both of these lures are on his front deck this time of year. Cox experimented with a longer frog rod this season and it helped him land a 3rd place finish at Wheeler Lake.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - John Garrett
programme.desc: John Garrett runs down the three baits that were key for his win on the Harris Chain of Lakes. Garrett rotated between these techniques depending on how the fish were positioned and their aggressiveness on the shell bar.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Emil Wagner
programme.desc: Emil Wagner sheds light on his favorite bait for winter fishing especially on spotted bass lakes like Lanier. With jig head minnows neko rigs and dropshots becoming popular everyone forgot about the shaky head.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Roberston
programme.desc: Matt Robertson talks about upsizing his spinnerbait and adjusting his blade sizes when throwing this lure in water temperatures varying from the 40's to 50's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Joey Cifuentes III
programme.desc: Joey Cifuentes tackles where the fish go when they finish spawning but the water temperatures aren't at their hottest yet like they will be later in the summer. Cifuentes dives into three different baits that are useful around lakes with standing timber for the last week of May as we head into June.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Clifford Pirch
programme.desc: Clifford Pirch gives us a few ways to rig a drop shot if you're specifically targeting smallmouth and spotted bass. Threading his worm on weedless is his ideal setup but when fishing for smallmouth and spotted bass they tend to be more open water and less obstructions around. That's when Pirch will opt for a few other methods for fall rate and action.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Joey Cifuentes III
programme.desc: Joey Cifuentes talks about the shallow nature of fish even when the temperatures are dropping across the country. The first feeling anglers have when the water temperatures drop is to fish deeper water but Cifuentes mentions how even in the Ozarks bass will hang out around shallow wood and rock still keyed in on a bigger meal that imitates dying baitfish.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Paul Marks
programme.desc: Paul Marks shows off his single bait that produced in two different situations depending on how he rigged it. The Zoom Fluke Stick in Natural Shad contributed almost all of his weight in his Elite victory at Lake Hartwell. His first approach was rigging it weightless to throw on shallow points where bass pushed blueback herring to feed in the morning then he switch to a shakey head in the afternoons.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jacob Foutz
programme.desc: Jacob Foutz walks us through his process of selecting sizes of jig heads when targeting bass in flooded timber. His sizes are as follows; 3/16 oz (5 to 10 feet) 1/4 oz (10 to 15 feet) 3/8 oz (20 feet and deeper). Foutz doesn't like getting any heavier than that if he can because of the leverage it gives fish to easily jump and throw the hook.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Seth Feider
programme.desc: Seth Feider goes through his wood jig and grass jig setup. He explains the differences in line tie and weed guard why he likes a short hook and his colors for flipping. Whether it's docks laydowns shoreline grass or submerged vegetation; Feider will often rely on a jig to get it done. His favorite size is a 5/8 ounce.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Kyle Welcher
programme.desc: Kyle Welcher gives his take on a few productive lures in the prespawn and how he balances their uses to be most effective while on the water. Should you use a Chatterbait where a jig could also work or vice versa he attacks this and more in this scenario.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Cory Johnston
programme.desc: Cory Johnston gives a quick bait breakdown of a key lure that helped him win the 2024 Bassmaster Elite Series event at the St. Lawrence River. Johnston battled the waves out in Lake Ontario on the final two days of the event to secure a win his second of the season.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Bob Downey
programme.desc: Bob Downey goes through what he would consider his spring selection for largemouth fishing. Spring means March and April in the south but can mean April May and June up north. Downey opts for a crankbait swim jig and two types of soft plastics when making the spring transition.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Stetson Blaylock
programme.desc: Stetson Blaylock explains a new bait he was introduced to that helps him catch not only deep northern smallmouth but also southern largemouth in the winter months. He also discusses the value in 2D sonar with this technique around structure in the south.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Matt Roberston
programme.desc: Matt Robertson talks about upsizing his spinnerbait and adjusting his blade sizes when throwing this lure in water temperatures varying from the 40's to 50's.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Austin Felix
programme.desc: Austin Felix gives his thoughts on when he picks up a Dropshot versus a Ned Rig and a Neko Rig. Speed is often the determining factor for each presentation and he tends to reserve the Neko for largemouth situations.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Shane LeHew
programme.desc: Shane LeHew talks about one of his favorite fun-fishing lures which is the Umbrella Rig aka Alabama Rig. LeHew utilizes this in multiple ways as he can cover water around shallow cover like he would with a spinnerbait but also with his electronics around deeper offshore structure.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Brad Whatley
programme.desc: Brad Whatley gives his strategy of covering water around the spawn when there is thicker cover present. Whatley winds his weighted swimbait around spawning areas and will trigger strikes or boils revealing where bass are positioned to catch on another tactic if necessary.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Patrick Walters
programme.desc: Elite Series Champion Patrick Walters gives the details of his approach at Lake Murray. Walters relied on a few baits throughout the week to win the event wire to wire. When fish were active and schooling Walters utilized a Zoom Super Fluke and a Rapala Jowler.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Timothy Dube
programme.desc: Tim Dube walks us through one of his favorite techniques in tournaments and fun fishing. Dube gives his take on practicing with a Glide Bait and his strategy to convert followers into fish that will commit to biting.

programme.desc: Logan Parks discusses a strategy he employed at Wheeler during his first Top 10. Varying line size can help crankbaits run different depth and retrieved faster or slower. It's something he recommends during the summer months when schools are forming offshore or have been fished for frequently.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Logan Latuso
programme.desc: Logan Latuso discusses a big key in the summer months...SHADE. This underrated aspect of the summer can get you some of the biggest bites of your day and it seemingly gets better as the day progresses. Take notes from Latuso and don't run your shade pattern too early to ensure some of your best success.

programme.title: Tackle Tip - Jake Whitaker
programme.desc: Jake Whitaker talks about the shallow bite windows that open up even with 100 degree days in the south. Whitaker leans on a topwater toad around any sort of cover that could hold fish. Anglers may get less bites in the heat of the summer but they can be the quality you need in a tournament.
